quote.text: -….when things seem to have reached that stage, merely say “I won’t play any longer”, and take your departure; but if you stay, stop lamenting.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that as a parent, not every battle needs to be fought—sometimes stepping back allows both you and your child to grow without the heavy burden of constant conflict.
    • Learn to let go of unproductive struggles in the family; when a situation becomes counterproductive, choose to withdraw gracefully rather than invest in lamentation that drains your energy.
  • Leadership
    • A wise leader discerns when an effort has reached its natural limit; rather than clinging to an approach that stifles progress, it is more virtuous to make a dignified exit from unproductive conflicts.
    • By halting endless lament over setbacks, you set an example of accountability and resilience, encouraging your team to adapt and evolve rather than dwell on the past.
  • Product Management
    • In product management, knowing when to stop investing in a failing strategy is essential—cut your losses early and redirect resources toward more promising opportunities.
    • Embrace each setback as a lesson rather than a loss; when a project reaches a dead end, decide to move on without regret, harnessing the experience to inspire future innovation.
